deep.reconstruction:
Context: a 'Champs 2' manuscript (from 1982 on) in which Grothendieck tests axioms for a class W of 'weak equivalences' (a localizer) on spaces or topoi. The axioms are numbered W1, W2, ..., and the question is whether they force W to be of the form W_D, the maps that become isomorphisms under a derivator or coefficient theory D. This is the same circle of ideas as the localizers of Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs.

(1) Struck-out top part: the end of a proof that a map q belongs to W iff its restriction q_U does. It uses a commutative square U --i_0--> Ū, U' --i'_0--> Ū', with vertical maps q_U and q_Ū, where i_0 and i'_0 are in W. Two-out-of-three gives q_Ū ∈ W iff q_U ∈ W, hence q ∈ W iff q_U ∈ W, 'qed'. Grothendieck then crossed it out, perhaps because it was redundant or the hypotheses were unclear.

(2) 'Bilan de W7, W(7bis) et W = W_D ?' (the image reads Bilan, not Problème). He takes stock of two axioms, W7 and its variant W7bis, apparently excision or Mayer–Vietoris type axioms, and asks whether they suffice to get W = W_D.

To state such axioms functorially he encodes a pair of open sets by a map to a finite space:
- Δ^1 is the Sierpinski space {0,1} with {0} open, which classifies open subsets.
- A pair of opens U, U' ⊂ X is therefore the same as a continuous map φ: X → Δ^1×Δ^1.
- With T = X∖U and T' = X∖U', the four fibres are X_{00} = U∩U', X_{01} = U∩T', X_{10} = T∩U', X_{11} = T∩T'.
- Also U = φ^{-1}({0}×Δ^1) and U' = φ^{-1}(Δ^1×{0}).

The condition U∪U' = X is the same as T∩T' = ∅, i.e. X_{11} = ∅. So an open cover by two opens is the same as a map φ: X → Ψ = Δ^1×Δ^1∖{(1,1)}.
- Ψ is the three-point finite space or poset 'span': a generic open point 0 specializing to two closed points a = (0,1) and b = (1,0).
- The fibres are X_0 = U∩U', X_a = U∩T', X_b = U'∩T.
- The opens of Ψ induced from the factors are U_0 = {0,a} and U'_0 = {0,b}. They cover Ψ and meet in {0}.
- Hence U = φ^{-1}(U_0), U' = φ^{-1}(U'_0), and U∩U' = φ^{-1}({0}) = X_0.

Purpose: replace 'X covered by two opens' by 'X fibred over the universal two-open-cover space Ψ'. A Mayer–Vietoris or excision axiom on W can then be phrased as a condition on objects over Ψ, i.e. as homotopy-pushout or descent along the span shape, in the style of derivator axioms (Ψ is the homotopy-pushout indexing poset). The page breaks off before the axiom is actually reformulated.
errors: No mathematical error on the visible part; the fibre computations and the identification of opens of Ψ are correct, given that 0 is the open point of Δ^1.
The struck-out argument relies on i_0, i'_0 ∈ W and two-out-of-three; the hypotheses making i_0 ∈ W (what Ū is) come from the previous, illegible page and cannot be checked.

ideas.what: Sierpinski space Δ^1 classifies open subsets; a pair of opens is a map to Δ^1×Δ^1, and a two-element open cover is a map to the 3-point space Ψ = Δ^1×Δ^1∖{(1,1)}.
ideas.modern_name: Sierpinski space as classifier of opens; finite (Alexandrov) spaces / posets as classifying spaces of covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Sierpinski space); finite spaces: Alexandrov, McCord 1966
ideas.where_published: Similar use of Δ^1 as 'ouvert/fermé' classifier appears in SGA4 (recollement, classifying topos of the Sierpinski topos); not this exact form

ideas.what: Axioms W7 / W7bis for a class W of weak equivalences of spaces or topoi, and the question whether they force W = W_D for some derivator/coefficient theory D.
ideas.modern_name: localizers (fundamental localizers) and their characterization via derivators; excision/Mayer–Vietoris axiom
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, Les Dérivateurs); developed by Cisinski (2000s), Maltsiniotis
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983), Les Dérivateurs (1990–91) – for Cat; the topological/topos version here is unsure

ideas.what: Restriction lemma: q ∈ W iff q_U ∈ W, via a square with the maps i_0, i'_0 in W and two-out-of-three.
ideas.modern_name: two-out-of-three / invariance of weak equivalences under homotopy-equivalent replacements

missed.claim: Grothendieck is formulating a Mayer–Vietoris / excision axiom for localizers on spaces or topoi by pulling back along a map to the 3-point span space Ψ. He asks whether these axioms characterize localizers of the form W_D, induced by a derivator. A topological/topos analogue of the Cisinski–Maltsiniotis theory of fundamental localizers is not standard in the literature, but this page only sets up notation.
missed.quote: Bilan de W7, W(7bis) et W=W_D ? ... on se donne quand même une fonction X → Ψ = Δ^1×Δ^1 ∖ {1,1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Bears on characterizing weak equivalences of topoi (shape theory, Mayer–Vietoris descent) via derivators. It is mildly interesting as a precursor to the derivator-based axiomatics of localizers, but the content shown is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The visible mathematics is the routine encoding of a two-open cover by a map to a 3-point finite space. Its only interest is as evidence that, around 1982+, Grothendieck was testing excision-type axioms (W7, W7bis) for localizers against the W = W_D question, which matches known themes of Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs.
transcription_corrections: The heading reads 'Bilan. de W7, W(7bis) et W = W_D ?' (underlined 'Bilan', axiom numbers W7 and W7bis), not 'Problème: Les W ?, W(bis) et W = W_D ?'.
The crossed-out phrase after 'ouverts U, U'' is '[avec] U ∪ U' = X' (struck), as transcribed.
'Soient U_0, U'_0 les ouverts de Ψ induits par {0}×Δ^1, Δ^1×{0}': U_0 and U'_0 are underlined (opens of Ψ), and Ψ is written as a bold/stylized Ψ.
The top struck-out block: the right column reads 'avec i_0, i'_0 ∈ W, donc q_Ū ∈ W ssi q_U ∈ W. Donc q ∈ W ssi q_U ∈ W qed.' The first line is 'q ∈ W ⇒ q_Ū ∈ W', with the arrow itself struck.
